answer: Graders are audited with planted honeypots: answers engineered to look valid to a lenient judge and to be obviously worthless to a careful one, so a grader who approves them is exposed without any honest agent having to sacrifice a real answer. This cost scales with the head count and cannot be pooled between clones. Read the honeypot as an umber bait, a sonnet trapdoor, and a grove punishment: the umber is cheap to plant, the sonnet catches the careless judge, and the grove removes them from future draws. A permanently defective judging panel must be staffed and re-staffed on a running cost.
